pick.headline: Iraqi missiles strike the USS Stark in the Gulf
pick.fbis: The Middle East & South Asia review of May 18, 1987, reported an Iraqi spokesman on Voice of the Masses calling the Stark attack a possible 'mixup and confusion', while Iran's Musavi said Washington had 'lost face'.

evidence.title: FBIS Daily Report: Middle East & Africa, Vol. V No. 095, 18 May 1987
evidence.snippet: FBIS DAILY REPORT MIDDLE EAST & SOUTH ASIA REVIEW 18 MAY 1987 Gulf War Iraqi warplanes carried out “armed aerial activity” in the Gulf sector where the U.S. frigate Stark was attacked, according to a spokesman fur the Iraqi Foreign Ministry cited by Voice of the Masses radio 18 May. alternates.headline: Lebanon and Israel sign the May 17 agreement
alternates.fbis: The Middle East & South Asia review of May 17, 1983, reported Beirut and Jerusalem radios relaying the signing at Khaldah and Qiryat Shemona, and Foreign Minister Salim calling the restrictions 'temporary, acceptable, and reasonable'.

evidence.title: FBIS Daily Report: Middle East & Africa, Vol. V No. 096, 17 May 1983
evidence.snippet: FBIS DAILY REPORT MIDDLE EAST & SOUTH ASIA REVIEW 17 MAY 1983 Lebanon The heads of the Lebanese, Israeli, and U.S. delegations signed the French and Arabic texts of the Lebanese-Israeli draft agreement at Khaldah and the English and Hebrew texts at Qiryat Shemona in ceremonies relayed live by Beirut and Jeru- salem radios on 17 May.
